text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code easier to read, understand, and maintain. During refactoring, developers might rename variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicate code. The behavior of the program stays exactly the same, so users do not notice any difference. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly and poorly. By refactoring regularly, teams keep their code clean and make future changes faster and safer.
